artists.biography:
"Kevin Robert Morby"  (born April 2, 1988) is an American musician, singer and songwriter. Formerly known as the bass guitarist of the folk rock band Woods and as the frontman of The Babies, Morby began a solo career in 2013.
Morby learned to play guitar when he was 10. In his teens he formed the band Creepy Aliens. At 17-year-old Morby dropped out of Blue Valley Northwest High School and moved from his native Kansas City to Brooklyn in the mid-2000s, supporting himself by working bike delivery and café jobs. He later joined the noise-folk group Woods on bass. While living in Brooklyn, he became close friends and roommates with Cassie Ramone of the punk trio Vivian Girls, and the two formed a side project together called The Babies, who released albums in 2011 and 2012.
Following his move to Los Angeles, Morby recorded a collection of songs with Babies producer Rob Barbato which were intended to be an homage to New York City. Released in 2013 by Woodsist Records, the eight-song collection was called Harlem River and became Morby's debut as a solo artist.

perplexity.description:
City Music is Kevin Morby's fourth studio album, released in 2017 on Dead Oceans. The record represents a significant shift in perspective from his previous work, functioning as an unapologetic celebration of metropolitan America filtered through an Americana and folk-rock lens. Recorded at Panoramic Studios in Stinson Beach between 2015 and 2016 and produced by Morby alongside Richard Swift, the album constructs a loose narrative centered on travel, urban belonging, and city life. Musically, the album builds momentum with locomotive-like propulsion, as evidenced in tracks like "Aboard My Train," with songs employing varied arrangements—from the delicate synths and woodwinds of "Come To Me Now" to the southern rock crescendo of the title track.

The album marks a deliberate departure from Morby's previous effort, Singing Saw, which explored introspective, cosmological themes in isolation. City Music instead captures the sensibility of someone writing on the road, presenting Morby as an awestruck traveler documenting his observations of American urban landscapes. The 48-minute collection spans twelve tracks that collectively evoke the experience of movement and discovery, balancing melancholic introspection with moments of exuberant celebration.

Critical reception was favorable, with the album earning a Metacritic score of 80 and receiving positive reviews from major publications. Pitchfork awarded it 8.1/10, while Uncut gave it 9/10, and Northern Transmissions rated it 8.4/10. The album solidified Morby's reputation as a distinctive voice in contemporary indie rock, demonstrating his ability to synthesize folk traditions with contemporary songwriting sensibilities.
